description: Self-hosted observability: metrics, logs, traces, dashboards and alerts. Stores data in PostgreSQL or ClickHouse. Accepts OpenTelemetry data.

summary.one_liner: DataCat is a self-hosted observability platform that stores metrics, logs, and distributed traces in PostgreSQL or ClickHouse and accepts OpenTelemetry and Datadog-compatible agent traffic.
summary.what_it_does: DataCat provides metrics exploration with formulas, dashboards and host maps, plus searchable logs with facets, live tail and trace correlation. It includes an APM service catalog, a trace explorer and waterfall view. Metric, log and trace monitors can send webhook or Slack notifications. Data intake accepts the Datadog public intake API and OTLP/HTTP (/v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs), and the README says a Datadog Agent 7.85.4 and 7.56.2 were tested. Accounts are local email/password with single-use invites and API/application keys. A single production process serves the API, web UI, installer and downloads.
use_cases: monitor application metrics and dashboards on my own servers
send OpenTelemetry data to a self-hosted backend
receive Datadog Agent data without a hosted account
set up alerts with Slack or webhook notifications
how_to_run: Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD and SESSION_SECRET in .env (e.g. with openssl rand), chmod 600 .env, and mkdir -p downloads
From source: corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10.11.0 --activate && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && BASE_PATH=/ pnpm run build:selfhost
From source: set DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET and PUBLIC_URL, then NODE_ENV=production PORT=3000 pnpm start
notable: Choice of PostgreSQL or ClickHouse for telemetry storage
Accepts Datadog Agent traffic and OTLP/HTTP without a hosted service
Built-in intake stats endpoint showing stored vs dropped items per intake path
Includes a benchmark kit that checks answers against known values
Schema migrates automatically on server start
caveats: Agent versions 7.57 to 7.84 are untested; agents sending unreadable trace formats receive a 422
Building from source requires Node 22.15+, pnpm 10.11.0 and PostgreSQL 14+; the agent requires Go 1.26.11+
Agent binaries and SDK packages are separate release assets that must be placed in downloads/ manually
Remote agent installs require setting PUBLIC_URL to an externally reachable HTTPS origin
